summary: Preinstall script downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload during npm install
details: The package's `package.json` declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers such as `_0x488df8`, per-function string dictionaries mapping short keys to literals like `"--version"`, `"/etc/os-release"`, `"bun"`). At install time it downloads the Bun runtime from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...zip`, extracts it to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` to run a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-compiled artifact (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header followed by string-array shuffle obfuscation using functions `WV8StW` and dictionary `n7gIxM`); its filename is unrelated to the package's stated Datadog RUM configuration purpose and its behavior cannot be inspected from source. Fetching an alternate language runtime at install time to execute an opaque obfuscated payload compiled for that runtime is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: it evades Node-oriented static analysis and yields arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine on `npm install`. The obfuscation of the lifecycle script itself, the runtime/payload name mismatch, and the requirement of a second runtime purely to execute bundled code are each independent indicators of evasion intent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
